1: ---
     2: # NIST 800-53 Gemara scan — all baselines (low / moderate / high).
     3: #
     4: # Flow per baseline:
     5: #   1. Export Gemara artifacts on the host  (delegate_to: localhost)
     6: #   2. Generate per-baseline Policy bundle  (delegate_to: localhost)
     7: #   3. Push bundle from host → VM registry  (delegate_to: localhost, via ansible_host IP)
     8: #   4. Write complytime.yaml on the VM
     9: #   5. complyctl get / generate / scan      (runs ON the VM, against the VM's own OS)
    10: #   6. Fetch results → host
    11: #
    12: # Usage (from utils/nist_sync/):
    13: #   ansible-playbook -i ansible/inventory.ini ansible/scan.yml
    14: #   ansible-playbook -i ansible/inventory.ini ansible/scan.yml -e baseline=moderate
    15: #
    16: # Optional variables:
    17: #   baseline      low | moderate | high | all  (default: all)
    18: #   product       rhel9                        (default: rhel9)
    19: #   base_profile  nist_800_53                  (default: nist_800_53)
    20: #   registry_port 5500                         (default: 5500)
    21: 
    22: - name: NIST 800-53 Gemara scan on RHEL9 VM
    23:   hosts: rhel9_scanner
    24:   become: true
    25:   vars:
    26:     product: "{{ lookup('env', 'PRODUCT') | default('rhel9', true) }}"
    27:     base_profile: "{{ lookup('env', 'BASE_PROFILE') | default('nist_800_53', true) }}"
    28:     registry_port: "{{ lookup('env', 'REGISTRY_PORT') | default('5500', true) }}"
    29:     # Resolve the list of baselines to test.
    30:     _baseline_arg: "{{ baseline | default(lookup('env', 'BASELINE') | default('all', true)) }}"
    31:     baselines: >-
    32:       {{ ['low', 'moderate', 'high'] if _baseline_arg == 'all'
    33:          else [_baseline_arg] }}
    34:     # Paths on the host machine.
    35:     # playbook_dir = .../utils/nist_sync/ansible — three levels below repo root.
    36:     repo_root: "{{ playbook_dir | realpath + '/../../..' }}"
    37:     gemara_dir: "{{ repo_root }}/build/gemara"
    38:     results_base: "{{ repo_root }}/build/complyctl-results/{{ product }}"
    39:     # complytime working directory inside the VM.
    40:     complyctl_home: /root/.complytime
    41: 
    42:   pre_tasks:
    43:     - name: Ensure host result directory exists
    44:       delegate_to: localhost
    45:       become: false
    46:       ansible.builtin.file:
    47:         path: "{{ results_base }}"
    48:         state: directory
    49:         mode: "0755"
    50: 
    51:     # Export once — covers all baselines.
    52:     - name: "Export Gemara artifacts for {{ product }} (host)"
    53:       delegate_to: localhost
    54:       become: false
    55:       ansible.builtin.command: >
    56:         python3 utils/nist_sync/export_to_gemara.py
    57:           --products {{ product }}
    58:           --output-dir build/gemara
    59:           --data-dir utils/nist_sync/data
    60:       args:
    61:         chdir: "{{ repo_root }}"
    62:       environment:
    63:         PYTHONPATH: "{{ repo_root }}"
    64: 
    65:     - name: Show exported files
    66:       delegate_to: localhost
    67:       become: false
    68:       ansible.builtin.find:
    69:         paths: "{{ gemara_dir }}"
    70:         recurse: true
    71:         patterns: "*.yaml"
    72:       register: exported
    73: 
    74:     - name: Gemara files exported
    75:       ansible.builtin.debug:
    76:         msg: "{{ exported.files | map(attribute='path') | map('replace', repo_root + '/', '') | list }}"
    77: 
    78:   tasks:
    79:     - name: Scan each baseline
    80:       ansible.builtin.include_tasks: tasks/scan_baseline.yml
    81:       loop: "{{ baselines }}"
    82:       loop_control:
    83:         loop_var: baseline_name
    84: 
    85:   post_tasks:
    86:     - name: Final results summary
    87:       delegate_to: localhost
    88:       become: false
    89:       ansible.builtin.find:
    90:         paths: "{{ results_base }}"
    91:         recurse: true
    92:         patterns: "*.xml,*.yaml"
    93:       register: all_results
    94: 
    95:     - name: Results written to host
    96:       ansible.builtin.debug:
    97:         msg: |
    98:           {{ all_results.files | length }} result file(s) under build/complyctl-results/{{ product }}/
    99:           {% for f in all_results.files | sort(attribute='path') %}
   100:           - {{ f.path | replace(repo_root + '/', '') }}
   101:           {% endfor %}

    76:   register: "haproxy_acme_remove_certs"
    77: 
    78: 
    79: ##############################################################################
    80: ## get new certs
    81: ##############################################################################
    82: - name: Check existence of acme CNAME records
    83:   ansible.builtin.command:
    84:     cmd: "dig +short -t CNAME '_acme-challenge.{{ item }}'"
    85:   register: haproxy_acme_cname
    86:   failed_when: "haproxy_acme_cname.stdout == ''"
    87:   changed_when: false
    88:   loop: "{{ haproxy_ssl_hosts }}"
    89:   become: false
    90:   delegate_to: "localhost"
    91:   check_mode: false  # this is safe run run, even in check mode
    92:   run_once: true
    93: 
    94: - name: Update certificates on one host at a time
    95:   throttle: 1
    96:   block:
    97:     - name: Issue the certificates using acme
    98:       ansible.builtin.command:
    99:         cmd: |
   100:           /home/acme/.acme.sh/acme.sh
   101:             --issue
   102:             --ecc
   103:             --keylength ec-256
   104:             --days "{{ haproxy_acme_renewal_days }}"
   105:             --dns dns_acmedns
   106:             --stateless
   107:             --dnssleep 3
   108:             --server "{{ haproxy_acme_server }}"
   109:             --domain "{{ item }}"
   110:             {{ acme_account.changed | ternary('--force', '') }}
   111:       environment:
   112:         ACMEDNS_BASE_URL: "{{ haproxy_acmedns.baseurl }}"
   113:         ACMEDNS_USERNAME: "{{ haproxy_acmedns.username }}"
   114:         ACMEDNS_PASSWORD: "{{ haproxy_acmedns.password }}"
   115:         ACMEDNS_SUBDOMAIN: "{{ haproxy_acmedns.subdomain }}"
   116:       loop: "{{ haproxy_ssl_hosts }}"
   117:       throttle: 1
   118:       register: "acme_issue"
   119:       changed_when: "acme_issue.rc == 0"
   120:       failed_when: 'acme_issue.rc != 0 and acme_issue.rc != 2'
   121:       become_user: "acme"
   122:       become: true
   123: 
   124:     # Now deploy the certificates to haproxy
   125:     # We do this in two steps:
   126:     # 1. Cold-deploy the certificates to haproxy's certs directory
   127:     # 2. Make sure haproxy is started, and hot-deploy the certificates to haproxy though the socket API
   128: 
   129:     - name: Cold-deploy the certificates to haproxy  # noqa: no-handler
   130:       ansible.builtin.command:
   131:         cmd: |
   132:           /home/acme/.acme.sh/acme.sh
   133:             --deploy
   134:             --deploy-hook haproxy
   135:             --domain "{{ item }}"
   136:       environment:
   137:         DEPLOY_HAPROXY_PEM_PATH: "/etc/haproxy/certs"
   138:       loop: "{{ haproxy_ssl_hosts }}"
   139:       register: "result"
   140:       changed_when: "result.rc == 0"
   141:       when: "acme_issue.changed"
   142:       become_user: "acme"
   143:       become: true
   144: 
   145:     - name: Start and enable haproxy
   146:       ansible.builtin.service:
   147:         name: "haproxy"
   148:         state: "started"
   149:         enabled: true
   150: 
   151:     - name: Wait for port 443 to become open  # noqa: no-handler
   152:       ansible.builtin.wait_for:
   153:         port: 443
   154:         delay: 5
   155:         host: "{{ haproxy_sni_ip.ipv4 }}"
   156:       when: "acme_issue.changed"
   157: 
   158:     - name: Hot-deploy the certificates to haproxy  # noqa: no-handler
   159:       ansible.builtin.command:
   160:         cmd: |
   161:           /home/acme/.acme.sh/acme.sh
   162:             --deploy
   163:             --deploy-hook haproxy
   164:             --domain "{{ item }}"
   165:       environment:
   166:         DEPLOY_HAPROXY_HOT_UPDATE: "yes"
   167:         DEPLOY_HAPROXY_STATS_SOCKET: "/var/lib/haproxy/haproxy.stats"
   168:         DEPLOY_HAPROXY_PEM_PATH: "/etc/haproxy/certs"
   169:       loop: "{{ haproxy_ssl_hosts }}"
   170:       when: "acme_issue.changed"
   171:       register: "result"
   172:       changed_when: "result.changed"
   173:       become_user: "acme"
   174:       become: true

    19:     - "/etc/logrotate.d/slapd"

    29: - name: Copying alternative service script

    32:     dest: "/etc/systemd/system/slapd.service"
    33:   notify:
    34:     - "systemd daemon-reload"
    35:     - "restart LDAP"
    36: 
    37: - name: force restart
    38:   meta: "flush_handlers"
    39: 
    40: - name: Ensure that a number of directories exist

    42:     path: "{{ item }}"
    43:     state: "directory"
    44:     owner: "{{ ldap_user }}"
    45:     group: "{{ ldap_group }}"
    46:     mode: "0755"
    47:   tags: "ldap"

    58:     - sczGroup.ldif
    59:     - groupOfMembers.ldif
    60:     - eduPerson.ldif
    61:     - ldapPublicKey.ldif
    62:     - eduMember.ldif
    63:     - voPerson.ldif
    64:     - sramPerson.ldif

    67:   template:
    68:     src: ldap.conf.j2
    69:     dest: "{{ ldap_dir }}/ldap.conf"
    70:     mode: "0644"
    71: 
    72: - name: Set indices
    73:   community.general.ldap_attrs:
    74:     dn: "olcDatabase={1}mdb,cn=config"
    75:     attributes:
    76:       olcDbIndex: "{{item}}"
    77:     state: "present"
    78:   with_items:
    79:     - "entryUUID eq"
    80:     - "o eq"
    81:     - "dc eq"
    82:     - "entryCSN eq"
    83: 
    84: - name: Set olcDatabase={-1}frontend olcSizeLimit
    85:   community.general.ldap_attrs:
    86:     dn: "olcDatabase={-1}frontend,cn=config"
    87:     state: "exact"
    88:     attributes:
    89:       olcSizeLimit: "unlimited"
    90: 
    91: - name: Set config

    93:     dn: "cn=config"
    94:     state: "exact"
    95:     attributes:
    96:       olcSizeLimit: "unlimited"
    97:       olcLogLevel: "{{ ldap_loglevel }}"
    98:       olcAttributeOptions: "time-"
    99:       olcTLSCertificateKeyFile: "{{ ssl_certs_dir }}/{{ internal_base_domain }}.key"
   100:       olcTLSCertificateFile: "{{ ssl_certs_dir }}/{{ internal_base_domain }}.crt"
   101:       olcTLSCACertificateFile: "{{ ssl_certs_dir }}/{{ internal_base_domain }}.crt"
   102:       olcTLSCipherSuite: >
   103:         SECURE256:-VERS-DTLS-ALL:-VERS-SSL3.0:-VERS-TLS1.0:-VERS-TLS1.1:-RSA:-DHE-RSA:-ECDHE-RSA
   104: 
   105: - name: Ensure the schemas are added to LDAP
   106:   ansible.builtin.script: "scripts/ldap-add {{ ldap_ldif_dir }}/{{ item }}"

   108:   failed_when: "result.rc not in [0,80]"
   109:   changed_when: "result.rc != 80"
   110:   loop:
   111:     - "sczGroup.ldif"
   112:     - "groupOfMembers.ldif"
   113:     - "eduPerson.ldif"
   114:     - "ldapPublicKey.ldif"
   115:     - "eduMember.ldif"
   116:     - "voPerson.ldif"
   117:     - "sramPerson.ldif"
   118: 
   119: - name: Setup Modules
   120:   community.general.ldap_attrs:
   121:     dn: cn=module{0},cn=config
   122:     attributes:
   123:       olcModuleLoad:
   124:         - back_monitor
   125:         - memberof
   126:         - refint
   127:         - dynlist
   128:         - syncprov
   129: 
   130: - name: Setup Monitor
   131:   community.general.ldap_entry:
   132:     dn: olcdatabase=monitor,cn=config
   133:     objectClass: olcDatabaseConfig
   134:     attributes:
   135:       olcRootDN: "cn=admin,cn=Monitor"
   136:       olcRootPW: "{{ '%s' | format(monitor_ldap_password) |  slapd_hash }}"
   137: 
   138: - name: Setup MemberOf(1)
   139:   community.general.ldap_entry:
   140:     dn: olcOverlay=memberof,olcDatabase={1}mdb,cn=config
   141:     objectClass:
   142:       - olcOverlayConfig
   143:       - olcMemberOf
   144:     attributes:
   145:       olcMemberOfRefInt: "TRUE"
   146:       olcMemberOfGroupOC: groupOfMembers
   147:       olcMemberOfMemberAD: member
   148:       olcMemberOfMemberOfAD: memberOf
   149: 
   150: - name: Setup MemberOf(2)
   151:   community.general.ldap_entry:
   152:     dn: olcOverlay=refint,olcDatabase={1}mdb,cn=config
   153:     objectClass:
   154:       - olcOverlayConfig
   155:       - olcRefintConfig
   156:     attributes:
   157:       olcRefintAttribute: memberof member
   158: 
   159: - name: Setup Dynlist
   160:   community.general.ldap_entry:
   161:     dn: olcOverlay=dynlist,olcDatabase={1}mdb,cn=config
   162:     objectClass:
   163:       - olcOverlayConfig
   164:       - olcDynamicList
   165:     attributes:
   166:       olcDlAttrSet: "{0}organizationalRole labeledURI roleOccupant"
   167: 
   168: - name: Setup Syncprov
   169:   community.general.ldap_entry:
   170:     dn: olcOverlay=syncprov,olcDatabase={1}mdb,cn=config
   171:     objectClass:
   172:       - olcOverlayConfig
   173:       - olcSyncProvConfig
   174:     attributes:
   175:       olcSpCheckpoint: 100 10
   176:       olcSpSessionLog: 100
   177: 
   178: - name: Setup main database
   179:   community.general.ldap_attrs:
   180:     dn: olcDatabase={1}mdb,cn=config
   181:     attributes:
   182:       olcSuffix: "{{ services_ldap.basedn }}"
   183:       olcRootDN: "{{ services_ldap.binddn }}"
   184:       olcRootPW: "{{ '%s' | format(services_ldap_password) |  slapd_hash }}"
   185:     state: exact
   186: 
   187: - name: Set root credentials
   188:   community.general.ldap_attrs:
   189:     dn: olcDatabase={0}config,cn=config
   190:     attributes:
   191:       olcAccess: >-
   192:           {0}to *
   193:           by dn.exact=gidNumber=0+uidNumber=0,cn=peercred,cn=external,cn=auth manage
   194:           {% if environment_name=="vm" %}
   195:           by dn.exact=gidNumber=1000+uidNumber=1000,cn=peercred,cn=external,cn=auth manage
   196:           {% endif %}
   197:           by dn.exact="{{ services_ldap.binddn }}" manage
   198:           by * break
   199:     state: exact
   200: 
   201: - name: Setup Syncrepl
   202:   community.general.ldap_attrs:
   203:     dn: olcDatabase={1}mdb,cn=config
   204:     attributes:
   205:       olcSyncrepl: >-
   206:         rid=001
   207:         provider="ldaps://{{ groups['ldap_primary'][0] }}/"
   208:         searchbase="{{ services_ldap.basedn }}"
   209:         type=refreshAndPersist
   210:         bindmethod=simple
   211:         binddn="{{ services_ldap.binddn }}"
   212:         credentials={{ services_ldap_password }}
   213:         retry="30 +"
   214:         timeout=30
   215:         network-timeout=5
   216:   when: inventory_hostname in groups['ldap_secondary']
   217: 
   218: - name: Get uid of openldap user
   219:   ansible.builtin.getent:
   220:     database: "passwd"
   221:     key: "openldap"
   222: 
   223: # store it in a nice var (so line below doesn't get too long)
   224: - name: Save gid of openldap user
   225:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:
   226:     openldap_auth: "gidNumber={{ansible_facts.getent_passwd['openldap'][2]}}+\
   227:                     uidNumber={{ansible_facts.getent_passwd['openldap'][1]}}"
   228: 
   229: - name: Set ACLs
   230:   community.general.ldap_attrs:
   231:     dn: "olcDatabase={1}mdb,cn=config"
   232:     attributes:
   233:       olcAccess:
   234:         - >-
   235:           to dn.regex="(([^,]+),{{ services_ldap.basedn }})$"
   236:           by dn.exact="{{ services_ldap.binddn }}" write
   237:           by dn.exact=gidNumber=0+uidNumber=0,cn=peercred,cn=external,cn=auth write
   238:           by dn.exact,expand="cn=admin,$1" read
   239:           by * break
   240:         - >-
   241:           to *
   242:           by dn.exact=gidNumber=0+uidNumber=0,cn=peercred,cn=external,cn=auth manage
   243:           by dn.exact={{openldap_auth}},cn=peercred,cn=external,cn=auth read
   244:           by dn.regex="cn=[^,]+,{{ services_ldap.basedn }}" read
   245:           {% if environment_name=="vm" %}
   246:           by dn.exact=gidNumber=1000+uidNumber=1000,cn=peercred,cn=external,cn=auth manage
   247:           {% endif %}
   248:           by * break
   249:         - >-
   250:           to attrs=userPassword
   251:           by self write
   252:           by anonymous auth
   253:           by * break
   254:     state: exact
   255:     ordered: true
   256: 
   257: - name: Initialize DIT
   258:   community.general.ldap_entry:
   259:     dn: "{{ services_ldap.basedn }}"
   260:     state: "present"
   261:     objectClass:
   262:       - "top"
   263:       - "dcObject"
   264:       - "organization"
   265:     attributes:
   266:       dc: "{{ services_ldap.basedn | regex_replace('^dc=([^,]+).*', '\\1') }}"
   267:       o: "{{ services_ldap.o }}"
   268:   when: inventory_hostname in groups['ldap_primary']
   269: 
   270: - name: Add ldap admins
   271:   include_tasks: "admins.yml"
   272:   when: >
   273:       inventory_hostname in groups['ldap_primary']
   274: 
   275: - name: Install backup script
   276:   template:
   277:     src: "ldap-backup.sh.j2"
   278:     dest: "{{backup_runparts}}/ldap-backup.sh"
   279:     mode: "0755"

     2: # The following variables will be set by the runner of this playbook:
     3: # projects_root: Global location for caching project checkouts and roles and collections
     4: #     should not have trailing slash on end

     6: # project_path: A simple join of projects_root/local_path folders
     7: # scm_url: https://server/repo
     8: # insights_url: Insights service URL (from configuration)
     9: # scm_branch: branch/tag/revision (HEAD if unset)
    10: # scm_clean: true/false
    11: # scm_username: username (only for svn/insights)
    12: # scm_password: password (only for svn/insights)
    13: # scm_accept_hostkey: true/false (only for git, set automatically)
    14: # scm_refspec: a refspec to fetch in addition to obtaining version
    15: # scm_track_submodules: true/false
    16: # roles_enabled: Value of the global setting to enable roles downloading
    17: # collections_enabled: Value of the global setting to enable collections downloading

    19: # awx_version: Current running version of the awx or tower as a string
    20: # awx_license_type: "open" for AWX; else presume Tower
    21: # gpg_pubkey: the GPG public key to use for validation, when enabled
    22: # client_id: Red Hat service account client ID; required for the 'service_account' authentication method used against the Insights API
    23: # client_secret: Red Hat service account client secret; required for the 'service_account' authentication method used against the Insights API

    28: - hosts: localhost

    30:   connection: local

    33:     - name: Delete project directory before update
    34:       ansible.builtin.shell: set -o pipefail && find . -delete -print | tail -2  # volume mounted, cannot delete folder itself
    35:       register: reg
    36:       changed_when: reg.stdout_lines | length > 1
    37:       args:
    38:         chdir: "{{ project_path }}"
    39:       tags:
    40:         - delete
    41: 
    42:     - name: Update project using git

    44:         - update_git

    46:         - name: Update project using git

    48:             dest: "{{ project_path | quote }}"

name: roles/maas/tasks/machines/update.yml
review_question: Is this Ansible artifact excessively large and in need of decomposition?
source_context:
1: ---
     2: # Purpose: Reconcile one existing MAAS machine against the inventory.
     3: # Called once per name in `_update_short` (built by _plan_sets.yml).
     4: # Skipped from machines.yml for any host whose status is "Deployed" — we
     5: # don't touch deployed machines.
     6: #
     7: # Step-by-step:
     8: #   1) Refresh interface facts for the node.
     9: #   2) If the node isn't in an edit-allowed state (Broken/Ready/New/Allocated),
    10: #      flag it Broken via _mark_broken.yml so we can edit interfaces.
    11: #      cleanup.yml will revert it at end of play.
    12: #   3) Walk `maas_interfaces` and reconcile each entry via _apply_one_iface.yml
    13: #      (parent NIC, MTU, native VLAN, tagged VLAN subinterfaces).
    14: #   4) Walk `maas_bonds` and reconcile each entry via _ensure_bond.yml.
    15: #   5) Read all subnets from MAAS, group by VLAN id, and link each interface
    16: #      whose MAC is in inventory to the right subnet via _apply_subnet.yml.
    17: #      Bonded-member physicals are excluded — MAAS won't link a subnet on an
    18: #      interface that's enslaved in a bond.
    19: #
    20: # Expects:
    21: #   - host                         : short hostname
    22: #   - inv_host                     : ansible inventory hostname
    23: #   - system_id                    : MAAS system_id
    24: #   - existing                     : MAAS object for this host (from
    25: #                                    maas_by_short)
    26: #   - system_status                : current MAAS status_name
    27: #   - hostvars[inv_host].maas_interfaces / .maas_bonds : the desired NIC and
    28: #                                                        bond layout
    29: #   - _maas_api, maas_auth_header
    30: # Returns: nothing.
    31: # Side effects: many — see the included helper files for details.
    32: 
    33: - name: Build OAuth header
    34:   include_tasks: ../_auth_header.yml
    35: 
    36: # 2) Record node system_id for downstream includes
    37: - name: Remember {{ inv_host }} = systemd id {{ system_id }}
    38:   set_fact:
    39:     _node_system_id: "{{ system_id }}"
    40: 
    41: # 5) Initialize desired structures so later tasks never explode on undefined
    42: # Load desired bonds & interfaces from group_vars
    43: - name: Load desired bonds & interfaces from group_vars
    44:   set_fact:
    45:     _desired_bonds: "{{ hostvars[inv_host].maas_bonds | default([]) }}"
    46:     _desired_ifaces: "{{ hostvars[inv_host].maas_interfaces | default([]) }}"
    47: 
    48: - include_tasks: _refresh_iface_facts.yml
    49: 
    50: - include_tasks: _mark_broken.yml
    51:   when: system_status not in ['Broken', 'Ready', 'New', 'Allocated']
    52: 
    53: - name: Apply interfaces (native_vid + tagged_vids)
    54:   include_tasks: _apply_one_iface.yml
    55:   loop: "{{ _desired_ifaces }}"
    56:   loop_control:
    57:     loop_var: desired_iface
    58:     label: "{{ desired_iface.prefix | default('(no prefix)') }}"
    59:   vars:
    60:     iface_obj: "{{ desired_iface }}"
    61: 
    62: # 9) Ensure bonds (each include runs per bond; no block-looping)
    63: - name: Ensure each bond
    64:   when: (_desired_bonds | default([])) | length > 0
    65:   include_tasks: _ensure_bond.yml
    66:   loop: "{{ _desired_bonds | default([]) }}"
    67:   loop_control:
    68:     loop_var: bond
    69:     label: "{{ bond.name | default('unnamed-bond') }}"
    70: 
    71: # Ensure we have fresh auth + base url
    72: - include_tasks: ../_auth_header.yml
    73: 
    74: # Read all interfaces for this node
    75: - name: Read machine interfaces (for subnet assignment)
    76:   uri:
    77:     url: "{{ _maas_api }}/nodes/{{ system_id }}/interfaces/"
    78:     method: GET
    79:     headers:
    80:       Authorization: "{{ maas_auth_header }}"
    81:       Accept: application/json
    82:     return_content: yes
    83:     status_code: 200
    84:   register: _ifaces_read
    85:   no_log: true
    86: 
    87: # INIT
    88: - name: Init iface list (id, name, vlan_id)
    89:   set_fact:
    90:     _iface_rows: []
    91: 
    92: # Build iface list (id, name, vlan_id, type) — bonds, vlans, physical NICs
    93: - name: Build iface list (id, name, vlan_id, type, mac)
    94:   set_fact:
    95:     _iface_rows: "{{ _iface_rows + [ {
    96:       'id': i.id,
    97:       'name': i.name,
    98:       'vlan_id': i.vlan.id,
    99:       'type': i.type,
   100:       'mac': (i.mac_address | default('') | lower)
   101:     } ] }}"
   102:   loop: >-
   103:     {{
   104:       _ifaces_read.json
   105:       | selectattr('vlan','defined')
   106:       | selectattr('vlan.id','defined')
   107:       | selectattr('type','defined')
   108:       | list
   109:     }}
   110:   loop_control:
   111:     loop_var: i
   112: 
   113: # Names of physical interfaces currently enslaved in a bond. MAAS rejects
   114: # link_subnet on these ("Cannot link interface(ethN) when interface is in a
   115: # bond"), so they must be excluded from the subnet pass below. The bond
   116: # itself (and its VLAN subinterfaces) carries the IP.
   117: - name: Collect bonded-member interface names
   118:   set_fact:
   119:     _bond_member_names: >-
   120:       {{
   121:         _ifaces_read.json
   122:         | selectattr('type', 'equalto', 'bond')
   123:         | map(attribute='parents') | flatten | unique | list
   124:       }}
   125: 
   126: # Bonds with no native VLAN: MAAS parks their untagged interface on the
   127: # parents' VLAN (e.g. bond100 lands on 1343 alongside bond25). Left in the
   128: # subnet pass, the CIDR match would assign that VLAN's IP to the bare bond
   129: # and collide with the interface that actually owns it. Only the bond's
   130: # tagged .NNNN children should get IPs, so exclude the bare bond by name.
   131: - name: Collect no-native bond names (their untagged iface takes no IP)
   132:   set_fact:
   133:     _no_native_bond_names: >-
   134:       {{
   135:         _desired_bonds
   136:         | rejectattr('native_vid', 'defined')
   137:         | map(attribute='name')
   138:         | list
   139:       }}
   140: 
   141: - include_tasks: ../_auth_header.yml
   142: 
   143: # Fetch ALL subnets once (we'll group them locally)
   144: - name: Read all subnets
   145:   uri:
   146:     url: "{{ _maas_api }}/subnets/"
   147:     method: GET
   148:     headers:
   149:       Authorization: "{{ maas_auth_header }}"
   150:       Accept: application/json
   151:     return_content: yes
   152:     status_code: 200
   153:   register: _all_subnets
   154:   no_log: true
   155: 
   156: - name: Init subnets_by_vlan map
   157:   set_fact:
   158:     _subnets_by_vlan: {}
   159: 
   160: # Build map: vlan_id -> [subnets...]
   161: - name: Group subnets by VLAN id
   162:   set_fact:
   163:     _subnets_by_vlan: >-
   164:       {{
   165:         _subnets_by_vlan | default({}) | combine({
   166:           (s.vlan.id|string):
   167:             (_subnets_by_vlan.get(s.vlan.id|string, []) + [s])
   168:         })
   169:       }}
   170:   loop: "{{ _all_subnets.json | default([]) }}"
   171:   loop_control:
   172:     loop_var: s
   173:   when: s.vlan is defined and s.vlan.id is defined
   174: 
   175: - name: Collect known MACs from inventory (any var ending in _mac)
   176:   set_fact:
   177:     _inv_macs: >-
   178:       {{
   179:         hostvars[inv_host]
   180:         | dict2items
   181:         | selectattr('key', 'search', '_mac$')
   182:         | map(attribute='value')
   183:         | map('lower')
   184:         | reject('equalto', '')
   185:         | list
   186:       }}
   187: 
   188: # Link subnets only on interfaces that can actually hold an IP: bonds, VLAN
   189: # subinterfaces, and standalone physicals. Bonded-member physicals share their
   190: # bond's MAC (so the _inv_macs match pulls them in), but they're filtered out
   191: # here by name via _bond_member_names.
   192: - name: Apply subnet assignment for each linkable iface we know from inventory
   193:   include_tasks: _apply_subnet.yml
   194:   loop: >-
   195:     {{
   196:       _iface_rows
   197:       | selectattr('mac', 'in', _inv_macs)
   198:       | rejectattr('name', 'in', _bond_member_names)
   199:       | rejectattr('name', 'in', _no_native_bond_names)
   200:       | list
   201:     }}
   202:   loop_control:
   203:     loop_var: row
   204:     label: "{{ row.name }} (vlan {{ row.vlan_id }})"
   205:   when:
   206:     - _iface_rows | length > 0
   207:   vars:
   208:     iface: "{{ row }}"
   209:     candidate_subnets: "{{ _subnets_by_vlan.get(row.vlan_id | string, []) }}"

   167:   block:
   168:     - name: Apply database migrations

   170:         cmd: "{{ nautobot_root }}/bin/nautobot-server migrate"

   190:       environment: "{{ nautobot_env }}"

   192:       changed_when: "'SUPERUSER_CHANGED' in nautobot_superuser.stdout"
   193:       become: true
   194:       become_user: "{{ nautobot_user }}"

   198:       ansible.builtin.include_tasks: readonly_token.yml
   199:       when: nautobot_token_publish_openbao | bool

   201:     - name: Publish a role-managed read-only MCP token to OpenBao
   202:       ansible.builtin.include_tasks: mcp_token.yml
   203:       when: nautobot_mcp_token_publish_openbao | bool

   205:     - name: Apply pending systemd reload before starting services
   206:       ansible.builtin.meta: flush_handlers
   207: 
   208:     - name: Enable and start the Nautobot services
   209:       ansible.builtin.systemd:
   210:         name: "{{ item }}"
   211:         state: started
   212:         enabled: true
   213:       loop:
   214:         - nautobot-server
   215:         - nautobot-worker
   216:         - nautobot-scheduler
   217: 
   218:     - name: Schedule the export Job via celery beat
   219:       ansible.builtin.command:
   220:         cmd: "{{ nautobot_root }}/bin/nautobot-server shell --interface python"
   221:         stdin: "{{ lookup('ansible.builtin.file', 'schedule_export.py') }}"
   222:       environment: >-
   223:         {{ nautobot_env | combine({
   224:              'NAUTOBOT_EXPORT_SCHEDULE_HOUR': nautobot_export_schedule_hour | string,
   225:              'NAUTOBOT_EXPORT_SCHEDULE_MINUTE': nautobot_export_schedule_minute | string}) }}
   226:       register: nautobot_schedule
   227:       changed_when: >-
   228:         {{ 'SCHEDULE_CREATED' in nautobot_schedule.stdout
   229:            or 'SCHEDULE_REENABLED' in nautobot_schedule.stdout }}
   230:       become: true
   231:       become_user: "{{ nautobot_user }}"
   232: 
   233:     # The export is the only thing that publishes this instance's inventory, and
   234:     # its ordering guard is what makes a stale artifact loud. Both are inert if
   235:     # the schedule is absent. Printing SCHEDULE_SKIPPED and letting the converge
   236:     # continue green lets the export stop publishing with nothing reporting it.
   237:     # A gate that reports its own failure as success is worse than no gate, so
   238:     # the converge fails here instead.
   239:     - name: Assert the export schedule was reconciled
   240:       ansible.builtin.assert:
   241:         that:
   242:           # Both halves are load-bearing. The negative catches a printed
   243:           # SCHEDULE_SKIPPED; the positive catches empty stdout, which would
   244:           # otherwise satisfy the negative and pass on no evidence at all.
   245:           - "'SCHEDULE_SKIPPED' not in nautobot_schedule.stdout"
   246:           - >-
   247:             'SCHEDULE_CREATED' in nautobot_schedule.stdout
   248:             or 'SCHEDULE_REENABLED' in nautobot_schedule.stdout
   249:             or 'SCHEDULE_EXISTS' in nautobot_schedule.stdout
   250:         fail_msg: >-
   251:           The export ScheduledJob was not reconciled: {{
   252:           nautobot_schedule.stdout | trim | default('(no output)', true) }}.
   253:           Without it nothing publishes the inventory artifact and the ordering
   254:           guard cannot fire. Fix the cause — do not skip this task.
   255:         quiet: true
   256: 
   257:     # Schedule the SSH-CLI discovery sweep (SSOTSyncDevices). Inert unless
   258:     # NAUTOBOT_ONBOARD_TARGETS is set — see the scope note in defaults/main.yml.
   259:     - name: Schedule the device-discovery Job via celery beat
   260:       ansible.builtin.command:
   261:         cmd: "{{ nautobot_root }}/bin/nautobot-server shell --interface python"
   262:         stdin: "{{ lookup('ansible.builtin.file', 'schedule_discovery.py') }}"
   263:       environment: >-
   264:         {{ nautobot_env | combine({
   265:              'NAUTOBOT_ONBOARD_TARGETS': nautobot_onboard_targets,
   266:              'NAUTOBOT_ONBOARD_PLATFORM': nautobot_onboard_platform,
   267:              'NAUTOBOT_ONBOARD_LOCATION': nautobot_onboard_location,
   268:              'NAUTOBOT_ONBOARD_PORT': nautobot_onboard_port | string,
   269:              'NAUTOBOT_DISCOVERY_SCHEDULE_HOUR': nautobot_discovery_schedule_hour | string,
   270:              'NAUTOBOT_DISCOVERY_SCHEDULE_MINUTE': nautobot_discovery_schedule_minute | string}) }}
   271:       register: nautobot_discovery_schedule
   272:       changed_when: "'DISCOVERY_SCHEDULED' in nautobot_discovery_schedule.stdout"
   273:       become: true
   274:       become_user: "{{ nautobot_user }}"
   275: 
   276:     - name: Wait for the Nautobot web UI to answer
   277:       ansible.builtin.uri:
   278:         url: "http://127.0.0.1:{{ nautobot_web_port }}/"
   279:         status_code: [200, 302]
   280:         follow_redirects: none
   281:       register: nautobot_health
   282:       until: nautobot_health.status in [200, 302]
   283:       retries: 20
   284:       delay: 6
   285:       changed_when: false
   286: 
   287:     # The seed jobs enqueue to the worker, which executes them with its
   288:     # EnvironmentFile. Flush any pending restart handler first (covers the
   289:     # nautobot.env-changed case)...
   290:     - name: Restart nautobot services before enqueuing jobs
   291:       ansible.builtin.meta: flush_handlers
   292: 
   293:     # ...and that is the whole mechanism. An unconditional worker restart used
   294:     # to follow, gated on nautobot_run_seed_jobs "so ordinary converges are
   295:     # untouched". Now that the flag defaults on, every converge is a seed run,
   296:     # so that restart would fire every time: permanently `changed`, and able to
   297:     # kill a scheduled job mid-flight.
   298:     #
   299:     # It is not needed. nautobot.env notifies the restart handler, so a changed
   300:     # env always bounces the worker in the same converge that changed it. A
   301:     # worker running stale env is therefore a real fault, and run_seed_jobs.py
   302:     # exits non-zero when any job is skipped, fails or times out — so it now
   303:     # surfaces as a failed converge instead of being papered over by a restart
   304:     # on every pass.
   305: 
   306:     # Load the seed bundle into Nautobot by running the additive SSoT DiffSync
   307:     # jobs (and, when NAUTOBOT_RUN_EXPORT is set, the export) once. On by
   308:     # default, paired with nautobot_build_seed, so every converge ingests the
   309:     # inventory it just resolved rather than replaying an aging bundle. The jobs
   310:     # are additive (create/update only), so re-running is safe. The worker
   311:     # executes them with the units' EnvironmentFile, so it already holds the
   312:     # seed-file path + export S3 credentials.
   313:     - name: Run the SSoT seed jobs (and optional export) once
   314:       ansible.builtin.command:
   315:         cmd: "{{ nautobot_root }}/bin/nautobot-server shell --interface python"
   316:         stdin: "{{ lookup('ansible.builtin.file', 'run_seed_jobs.py') }}"
   317:       environment: >-
   318:         {{ nautobot_env | combine({'NAUTOBOT_RUN_EXPORT': nautobot_run_export | string}) }}
   319:       register: nautobot_run_seed
   320:       # A job that FAILED also prints JOB_DONE (with status FAILURE), so match
   321:       # the status too — otherwise a failed run reports `changed`.
   322:       changed_when: nautobot_run_seed.stdout is search('JOB_DONE .+ SUCCESS')
   323:       become: true
   324:       become_user: "{{ nautobot_user }}"
   325:       when: nautobot_run_seed_jobs | bool

review_question: Is this Ansible artifact excessively large and in need of decomposition?
source_context:
1: ---
     2: # Gateway collector — OpenTelemetry-recommended "gateway pattern" implementation.
     3: # Called from setup.yml when `opentelemetry_gateway_enabled: true`, *before*
     4: # the helm task so the gateway collector spec AND its supporting resources
     5: # (htpasswd Secret + Ingress) are included in the chart values.
     6: #
     7: # All resources go through helm via:
     8: #   - `collectors.<gateway_name>` (the OpenTelemetryCollector CR + the
     9: #     operator-spawned Service/Deployment) → driven by
    10: #     `opentelemetry_collectors[<gateway_name>]`
    11: #   - `extraObjects[]` (Secret + Ingress) → driven by
    12: #     `opentelemetry_additional_config.extraObjects`
    13: #
    14: # That way helm owns the full lifecycle: a `helm upgrade` after disabling
    15: # the gateway tears everything down, and credential rotation is reflected
    16: # through a pod-annotation checksum so the operator triggers a rollout.
    17: 
    18: - name: "Compute gateway derived values"
    19:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    20:     _opentelemetry_gateway_full_name: "{{ opentelemetry_release_name }}-{{ opentelemetry_gateway_name }}"
    21:     _opentelemetry_gateway_htpasswd_secret_name: "{{ opentelemetry_release_name }}-{{ opentelemetry_gateway_name }}-htpasswd"
    22:     _opentelemetry_gateway_auth_enabled: "{{ (opentelemetry_gateway_htpasswd | default('') | length) > 0 }}"
    23: 
    24: - name: "Build the gateway collector spec"
    25:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    26:     opentelemetry_collectors: >-
    27:       {{
    28:         (opentelemetry_collectors | default({}))
    29:         | combine({ opentelemetry_gateway_name: _opentelemetry_gateway_collector_spec }, recursive=True)
    30:       }}
    31:   vars:
    32:     _volumes: >-
    33:       {{
    34:         [{
    35:           'name': 'htpasswd',
    36:           'secret': {'secretName': _opentelemetry_gateway_htpasswd_secret_name}
    37:         }]
    38:         if _opentelemetry_gateway_auth_enabled else []
    39:       }}
    40:     _volume_mounts: >-
    41:       {{
    42:         [{
    43:           'name': 'htpasswd',
    44:           'mountPath': '/etc/otel-auth',
    45:           'readOnly': true
    46:         }]
    47:         if _opentelemetry_gateway_auth_enabled else []
    48:       }}
    49:     # Credential rotation: the basicauth/server extension caches the
    50:     # htpasswd file at startup, so secret content changes only take effect
    51:     # when the pod restarts. Putting a checksum of the content in
    52:     # podAnnotations makes the operator roll the pod whenever the content
    53:     # differs from the previous apply.
    54:     _pod_annotations: >-
    55:       {{
    56:         {'checksum/htpasswd': (opentelemetry_gateway_htpasswd | hash('sha256'))}
    57:         if _opentelemetry_gateway_auth_enabled else {}
    58:       }}
    59:     _extensions: >-
    60:       {{
    61:         {'basicauth/server': {'htpasswd': {'file': '/etc/otel-auth/htpasswd'}}}
    62:         if _opentelemetry_gateway_auth_enabled else {}
    63:       }}
    64:     _service_extensions: >-
    65:       {{
    66:         ['basicauth/server']
    67:         if _opentelemetry_gateway_auth_enabled else []
    68:       }}
    69:     # Auto-wire basicauth/server onto the OTLP HTTP receiver. We deep-merge
    70:     # so the user keeps full control of receiver options (compression,
    71:     # max_recv_msg_size, …).
    72:     _otlp_http_auth_overlay:
    73:       otlp:
    74:         protocols:
    75:           http:
    76:             auth:
    77:               authenticator: "basicauth/server"
    78:     _receivers: >-
    79:       {{
    80:         opentelemetry_gateway_receivers
    81:         | combine(_otlp_http_auth_overlay, recursive=True)
    82:         if _opentelemetry_gateway_auth_enabled
    83:         else opentelemetry_gateway_receivers
    84:       }}
    85:     # If the user did not provide explicit pipelines, route every receiver +
    86:     # processor + exporter into metrics & logs pipelines. Works for the
    87:     # common case of homogeneous OTLP exporters; override when you have
    88:     # signal-specific routing.
    89:     _default_pipelines:
    90:       metrics:
    91:         receivers: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_receivers.keys() | list }}"
    92:         processors: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_processors.keys() | list }}"
    93:         exporters: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_exporters.keys() | list }}"
    94:       logs:
    95:         receivers: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_receivers.keys() | list }}"
    96:         processors: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_processors.keys() | list }}"
    97:         exporters: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_exporters.keys() | list }}"
    98:     _pipelines: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_pipelines if (opentelemetry_gateway_pipelines | length > 0) else _default_pipelines }}"
    99:     _opentelemetry_gateway_collector_spec:
   100:       enabled: true
   101:       mode: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_mode }}"
   102:       replicas: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_replicas }}"
   103:       # Predictable service name (`<release>-<gateway_name>-collector`),
   104:       # otherwise the chart defaults to `<release>-collector` which
   105:       # collides with any other non-daemon collector. Required for the
   106:       # Ingress backend reference below.
   107:       fullnameOverride: "{{ _opentelemetry_gateway_full_name }}"
   108:       resources: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_resources }}"
   109:       volumes: "{{ _volumes }}"
   110:       volumeMounts: "{{ _volume_mounts }}"
   111:       podAnnotations: "{{ _pod_annotations }}"
   112:       config:
   113:         extensions: "{{ _extensions }}"
   114:         receivers: "{{ _receivers }}"
   115:         processors: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_processors }}"
   116:         exporters: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_exporters }}"
   117:         service:
   118:           extensions: "{{ _service_extensions }}"
   119:           pipelines: "{{ _pipelines }}"
   120: 
   121: - name: "Inject the gateway Secret + Ingress as chart extraObjects"
   122:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:
   123:     opentelemetry_additional_config: >-
   124:       {{
   125:         (opentelemetry_additional_config | default({}))
   126:         | combine({
   127:             'extraObjects': (
   128:               ((opentelemetry_additional_config | default({})).extraObjects | default([]))
   129:               + _gateway_extra_objects
   130:             )
   131:           })
   132:       }}
   133:   when: _gateway_extra_objects | length > 0
   134:   vars:
   135:     _htpasswd_secret_obj:
   136:       apiVersion: "v1"
   137:       kind: "Secret"
   138:       metadata:
   139:         name: "{{ _opentelemetry_gateway_htpasswd_secret_name }}"
   140:         namespace: "{{ opentelemetry_namespace }}"
   141:       type: "Opaque"
   142:       stringData:
   143:         htpasswd: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_htpasswd }}"
   144:     _ingress_obj:
   145:       apiVersion: "networking.k8s.io/v1"
   146:       kind: "Ingress"
   147:       metadata:
   148:         name: "{{ _opentelemetry_gateway_full_name }}"
   149:         namespace: "{{ opentelemetry_namespace }}"
   150:         annotations: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_ingress_annotations }}"
   151:       spec:
   152:         ingressClassName: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_ingress_class_name }}"
   153:         tls: >-
   154:           {{
   155:             [{
   156:               'hosts': [opentelemetry_gateway_ingress_hostname],
   157:               'secretName': opentelemetry_gateway_ingress_tls_secret_name
   158:             }]
   159:             if opentelemetry_gateway_ingress_tls_enabled else []
   160:           }}
   161:         rules:
   162:           - host: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_ingress_hostname }}"
   163:             http:
   164:               paths:
   165:                 - path: "/"
   166:                   pathType: "Prefix"
   167:                   backend:
   168:                     service:
   169:                       name: "{{ _opentelemetry_gateway_full_name }}-collector"
   170:                       port:
   171:                         name: "otlp-http"
   172:     _gateway_extra_objects: >-
   173:       {{
   174:         ([_htpasswd_secret_obj] if _opentelemetry_gateway_auth_enabled else [])
   175:         + ([_ingress_obj] if opentelemetry_gateway_ingress_enabled else [])
   176:       }}

     2: - name: Setup non-root User
     3:   gather_facts: no

    10:       local_undercloud_pubkey: "{{ inventory_dir }}/id_rsa_undercloud.pub"
    11:       default_privatekey: "~/.ssh/id_rsa"
    12:       default_pubkey: "{{ default_privatekey }}.pub"

    15:       - name: sudoers no tty
    16:         lineinfile:
    17:             dest: /etc/sudoers
    18:             state: absent
    19:             regexp: 'Defaults\s+requiretty'
    20: 
    21:       - name: create default user
    22:         user:
    23:             name: "{{ install.user.name }}"
    24:             state: present
    25:             password: "{{ install.user.password | password_hash('sha512') }}"
    26: 
    27:       - name: add user to sudoers
    28:         lineinfile:
    29:             dest: "/etc/sudoers"
    30:             line: "{{ install.user.name }} ALL=(root) NOPASSWD:ALL"
    31: 
    32:       - name: create .ssh directory for non-root user
    33:         file:
    34:             path: "{{ default_privatekey | dirname }}"
    35:             state: directory
    36:         register: user_ssh_dir
    37:         become_user: "{{ install.user.name }}"
    38:         become: yes
    39: 
    40:       - block:
    41:           - name: inject local private key to undercloud
    42:             copy:
    43:                 src: "{{ ansible_ssh_private_key_file }}"
    44:                 # Workaround due to https://github.com/ansible/ansible/issues/21145
    45:                 dest: "{{ user_ssh_dir.path }}/{{ default_privatekey | basename }}"
    46:                 mode: 0600
    47:                 owner: "{{ install.user.name }}"
    48:                 group: "{{ install.user.name }}"
    49:                 force: yes
    50:             register: key_injection
    51: 
    52:           - name: Retrieve public key from private key
    53:             shell: "ssh-keygen -y -f {{ default_privatekey }} > {{ default_pubkey }}"
    54:             become_user: "{{ install.user.name }}"
    55:             become: yes
    56: 
    57:           - name: Retrieve public key from private key to localhost
    58:             shell: "ssh-keygen -y -f {{ ansible_ssh_private_key_file }} > {{ local_undercloud_pubkey }}"

    68:                 force: yes

    70:                 - "{{ default_privatekey }}"
    71:                 - "{{ default_pubkey }}"

name: src/clawrium/platform/registry/zeroclaw/playbooks/tasks/pair.yaml
review_question: Is this Ansible artifact excessively large and in need of decomposition?
source_context:
1: ---
     2: # Reusable pair-handshake task file (issue #437, locked-pair fix #445).
     3: #
     4: # Every lifecycle op that brings the zeroclaw daemon up MUST include this
     5: # file. There is no skip path.
     6: #
     7: # Two-branch state machine, picked off the /pair/code response shape:
     8: #
     9: #   1. Fresh daemon (no row in devices.db) -> GET /pair/code returns a
    10: #      non-null pairing_code. Use it directly.
    11: #   2. Locked daemon (devices.db has prior rows, survives systemctl
    12: #      restart) -> GET /pair/code returns {"pairing_code": null}. POST
    13: #      to /api/pairing/initiate with the existing bearer to mint a fresh
    14: #      code, then continue down the same POST /pair path.
    15: #
    16: # Both branches converge on the existing X-Pairing-Code exchange.
    17: #
    18: # Inputs:
    19: #   - gateway_local_base: http://127.0.0.1:<port> (set by including playbook)
    20: #   - ansible_host, gateway_port (used to emit zeroclaw_gateway_url fact)
    21: #   - agent_name, agent_type (used in failure messages)
    22: #   - config.gateway.auth: current Bearer from hosts.json. Required only
    23: #     when /pair/code returns null. May be empty/undefined on first install
    24: #     (when the locked branch cannot fire anyway).
    25: #
    26: # Outputs (cacheable host facts; configure_agent / restart_agent read these
    27: # out of artifacts/<run>/fact_cache):
    28: #   - zeroclaw_gateway_token: bearer token minted by /pair
    29: #   - zeroclaw_gateway_url:   ws://<host>:<port>/ws/chat
    30: 
    31: - name: Request pairing code (fresh-boot branch)
    32:   ansible.builtin.uri:
    33:     url: "{{ gateway_local_base }}/pair/code"
    34:     method: GET
    35:     status_code: 200
    36:     timeout: 10
    37:     return_content: yes
    38:   register: pair_code_response
    39:   no_log: true
    40: 
    41: # Locked branch: zeroclaw v0.7.5's /pair/code returns
    42: # {"pairing_code": null, "pairing_required": true} once devices.db has any
    43: # prior row. The authenticated initiate endpoint mints a fresh code that
    44: # the existing POST /pair task below can consume unchanged.
    45: #
    46: # ATX B2: explicitly accept 401 and 503 so the recovery path produces an
    47: # actionable operator message instead of a raw `Status code was 401`
    48: # Ansible error. The `Validate locked-branch initiate response` task below
    49: # then fails with explicit guidance to re-run `clawctl agent configure` (401)
    50: # or check daemon health (503).
    51: - name: Mint pairing code via /api/pairing/initiate (locked-pair branch)
    52:   ansible.builtin.uri:
    53:     url: "{{ gateway_local_base }}/api/pairing/initiate"
    54:     method: POST
    55:     status_code: [200, 401, 503]
    56:     timeout: 10
    57:     headers:
    58:       Authorization: "Bearer {{ config.gateway.auth | default('') }}"
    59:     return_content: yes
    60:   register: initiate_response
    61:   no_log: true
    62:   when:
    63:     - pair_code_response.json is defined
    64:     - pair_code_response.json.pairing_code is none
    65: 
    66: # ATX B2: surface 401/503 as actionable operator messages BEFORE the
    67: # resolved_pairing_code set_fact runs, so the operator sees the right
    68: # remediation instead of a generic "pairing code" failure downstream.
    69: #
    70: # ATX iter-3 NB2: this task MUST NOT carry `no_log: true`. The
    71: # lifecycle.py censored-event handler (W1) skips events where
    72: # `res.censored` is set, which silently swallows the operator-actionable
    73: # branching this msg encodes. The current msg references only
    74: # `initiate_response.status` (an int — safe to log) plus the constants
    75: # `agent_name` and `agent_type`. Future editors:
    76: #
    77: #   WARNING: do NOT reference `initiate_response.json` or
    78: #   `initiate_response.content` in this msg. A debug-mode daemon may echo
    79: #   the Authorization header back in its 401 body; templating that into
    80: #   the msg would leak the bearer through the fail-msg path that bypasses
    81: #   no_log.
    82: - name: Validate locked-branch initiate response
    83:   ansible.builtin.fail:
    84:     msg: >-
    85:       {% if initiate_response.status == 401 %}POST /api/pairing/initiate
    86:       returned 401: the bearer in hosts.json is stale (likely because
    87:       devices.db was wiped or rebuilt on the host). Run
    88:       `clawctl agent configure {{ agent_name }}` to re-pair from scratch.
    89:       {% elif initiate_response.status == 503 %}POST /api/pairing/initiate
    90:       returned 503: zeroclaw daemon reports pairing disabled or unavailable.
    91:       Check `journalctl --unit {{ agent_type }}-{{ agent_name }}` and restart
    92:       the daemon, then re-run `clawctl agent configure {{ agent_name }}`.
    93:       {% else %}POST /api/pairing/initiate returned an unexpected status
    94:       {{ initiate_response.status }} — see daemon logs.
    95:       {% endif %}
    96:   when:
    97:     - initiate_response is defined
    98:     - initiate_response.status is defined
    99:     - initiate_response.status != 200
   100: 
   101: - name: Resolve pairing code from whichever branch produced one
   102:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:
   103:     resolved_pairing_code: >-
   104:       {{
   105:         (initiate_response.json.pairing_code
   106:           if (pair_code_response.json is defined
   107:               and pair_code_response.json.pairing_code is none
   108:               and initiate_response is defined
   109:               and initiate_response.json is defined)
   110:           else pair_code_response.json.pairing_code)
   111:         if pair_code_response.json is defined else none
   112:       }}
   113:   no_log: true
   114: 
   115: # Do NOT set `no_log: true` on this fail task. The msg body is pure
   116: # template-literal text (`agent_name`, `agent_type` — both safe to log).
   117: - name: Validate pairing code shape
   118:   ansible.builtin.fail:
   119:     msg: >-
   120:       Neither GET /pair/code nor POST /api/pairing/initiate returned a usable
   121:       pairing code. Check daemon logs:
   122:       `journalctl --unit {{ agent_type }}-{{ agent_name }}`. If devices.db was
   123:       wiped externally, run `clawctl agent configure {{ agent_name }}` after
   124:       restoring it.
   125:   when:
   126:     - resolved_pairing_code is not defined
   127:       or resolved_pairing_code is none
   128:       or resolved_pairing_code | length < 1
   129: 
   130: # ATX W2: declared format guard for the pairing code before it enters the
   131: # X-Pairing-Code HTTP header. Python's http.client already rejects CRLF in
   132: # header values since 3.4, so this is preventative rather than load-bearing;
   133: # the regex also documents the contract (alphanumeric/_/- max 128 chars) so
   134: # a future caller can't silently reuse the value in a shell command or URL
   135: # path without re-validating.
   136: - name: Validate pairing code format
   137:   ansible.builtin.fail:
   138:     msg: >-
   139:       Pairing code returned by the daemon has an unexpected format. Daemon
   140:       logs: `journalctl --unit {{ agent_type }}-{{ agent_name }}`.
   141:   when:
   142:     - resolved_pairing_code is not match('^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,128}$')
   143: 
   144: # ZeroClaw v0.7.5 expects the one-time code via the `X-Pairing-Code` HTTP
   145: # header (per the daemon's startup banner), not a JSON body.
   146: - name: Exchange pairing code for bearer token
   147:   ansible.builtin.uri:
   148:     url: "{{ gateway_local_base }}/pair"
   149:     method: POST
   150:     status_code: 200
   151:     timeout: 10
   152:     headers:
   153:       X-Pairing-Code: "{{ resolved_pairing_code }}"
   154:     return_content: yes
   155:   register: pair_response
   156:   no_log: true
   157: 
   158: - name: Validate bearer token shape
   159:   ansible.builtin.fail:
   160:     msg: >-
   161:       /pair did not return a usable token. Daemon logs:
   162:       `journalctl --unit {{ agent_type }}-{{ agent_name }}`. Re-run
   163:       `clawctl agent configure {{ agent_name }}` after fixing the daemon.
   164:   when:
   165:     - pair_response.json is not defined
   166:       or pair_response.json.token is not defined
   167:       or pair_response.json.token is none
   168:       or pair_response.json.token | length < 16
   169: 
   170: # Emit gateway token + URL as cacheable host facts. The Python caller reads
   171: # them out of artifacts/<run>/fact_cache and persists them to hosts.json
   172: # under agents.<n>.config.gateway.{auth,url}. Mirrors the OpenClaw
   173: # fact-emission pattern in install.py:307-316. `no_log: true` so the value
   174: # isn't echoed at -vvv.
   175: - name: Save gateway credentials as cacheable facts
   176:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:
   177:     zeroclaw_gateway_token: "{{ pair_response.json.token }}"
   178:     zeroclaw_gateway_url: "ws://{{ ansible_host }}:{{ gateway_port }}/ws/chat"
   179:     cacheable: true
   180:   no_log: true
